text:
maria: rolling BMC firmware patch started in us-west-1 at 08:12 UTC, noticed odd sensor behaviour, nodes failing provision checks

alex: details? which patch?

maria: `bmc-fw-2026.03-acpi-therm-override` on dedicated racks. After ~30min we see IPMI query timeouts and a lot of `sensor coalescing` in the bmc logs. gpu provisioner backlog + autoscaler churn.

kevin: seen that pattern before. ACPI override can collapse some sensor streams so IPMI responses bundle, resulting in long poll times. Any secureboot toggles during this rollout?

maria: no secureboot flips in this job. but a subset of nodes reported `UEFI var write failed` immediately before the BMC started spamming:
```
[2026-03-20T08:18:12Z] uefi: write_var(secure_boot) -> -EIO
[2026-03-20T08:18:12Z] bmc: ipmi timeout after 5s for node rack-131
```

jess: that's nasty. Provisioner logs show `provisioner: attach-gpu timed out` and retries piling up. capacity for gpu pools in us-west-1 down ~11%.

leo: can we pause the rollout and roll back the BMC FW for the affected host class?

deploy-bot: rolling-update job 2026-03-20-08:10 active -> PAUSE requested by jess

maria: paused cluster-wide. starting targeted rollback for rack series `r131-*` and `r132-*`. prep commands below.

maria: runbook snippet to rollback BMC image via oob jumphost:
```
ssh oob-usw1-ops
for host in r131-01 r131-02 r132-03; do
  ipmitool -I lanplus -H $host -U admin -P **** sol deactivate
  ipmitool -I lanplus -H $host -U admin -P **** fwumpload rollback bmc-fw-2025.11
done
```

kevin: while rolling back, we should mark the affected racks as `no-provision` in fleet-provisioner to avoid thrash. I'll push a short-lived policy: `provisioner.exclude=r131*,r132*`.

jess: tagging this as infrastructure-incident, postmortem required. Oncall, please coordinate with platform to shift critical jobs to eu-west-2 until capacity stabilises.

oncall-sre: acknowledged. shifting realtime inference lanes off us-west-1 now. ETA 10m.

alex: curious — why did UEFI var write fail without explicit secureboot toggles? hypothesis: ACPI thermal override modifies UEFI runtime services timing, causing varstore commit to hit EIO under load. That then leaves some nodes with inconsistent UEFI state which BMC then flags during a health poll.

maria: agree. also seeing `bmc: sensor overflow, coalesced 42 samples` in the dumps. IPMI query latency distribution: median 120ms -> p99 9.2s. provisioner p99 waited 10s before marking node dead.

leo: cost impact: with ~11% GPU capacity down and jobs rescheduled to on-demand dedicated hosts in other regions, we estimate ~$1,200/hr incremental for next 6hrs if rollback slow. need to weigh quick rollback vs controlled remediation.

kevin: mitigation plan: 1) rollback BMC image for affected racks (in progress) 2) mark racks no-provision 3) drain in-flight allocations gracefully 4) throttle provisioner retry backoff to reduce pressure 5) schedule focused firmware QA for ACPI paths

maria: executing step 1 now. reporting progress.

sre-bot: alert: fleet-provisioner backlog increased to 1,340 tasks (baseline 120) at 08:23 UTC -> autoscaler bumped +5 nodes to meet demand

jess: please paste any failing IPMI calls here for debugging. also add nodes to a temp monitoring dashboard (oob-health-acpi).

maria: sample failing ipmi call:
```
ipmitool -I lanplus -H r131-02 -U admin -P **** sdr elist
Error: Connection timed out
```

alex: thanks. can we try a lower-frequency IPMI probe to avoid coalescing? change from 5s -> 30s for oob-poller for those racks.

kevin: applied `oob.poll.interval=30s` for r131*, r132*. should cut the p99 poll storms.

maria: rollback completed for r131-01..04 and r132-01..02, health checks are returning green for IPMI and UEFI varstore now. provisioning backlog dropping.

sre-bot: info: fleet-provisioner backlog 220 tasks at 08:41 UTC. autoscaler scaling actions stabilizing.

jess: nice work. next steps: full postmortem, add a preflight ACPI/UEFI sanity check to the firmware rollout job, and schedule a canary with extended oob polling before mass rollout.

leo: will draft cost impact note for finance. pls include exact downtime windows and affected capacity by minute.

maria: adding logs + runbook updates to the incident doc. thanks all for quick action. :heart:
